review_comments.body: for what it's worth, the existing implementation seemed to use this as well

but.. how?

What does passing the empty string to `argv[1]` and the string `${pkgs.blah}/bin/blah  some-args` as `argv[1]` even mean?

Something very funky is going on here no? `""` is not a valid  execcutable and neither is `"/nix/store-xx/bin/blah args"` (notice the space).

I'm not sure how to read this.

fwiw I expected this to be:

```
process.argv = [  (lib.getExe cfg.package) args ];
```

Oooooh! We're trying to do:

```

        ExecStart = [
          ""
          "${lib.getExe cfg.package} ${args}"
        ];
```


But that means something different. As  `process.argv` is escaped iirc?

I think this needs to be:

```
# reset the ExecStart 
systemd.service.serviceConfig.ExecStart = lib.mkBefore [""];
# set argv
process.argv = [ (lib.getExe cfg.package) args ];
```

instead

This is because the default value of `ExecStart` is

```
    ExecStart = [
          (escapeSystemdExecArgs config.process.argv)
        ];
```

which would simply expand to

```
   ExecStart = "  ''  '/nix/store/xxx-redlib/bin/redlib --arg1 --arg2'";
```

which is wrong and not equivalent to the original file
Thank you both, I didn't know what that was about, so I just kept it, hoping someone else would know about it.

Maybe just an alias without warnings for now?

```suggestion
        mkAliasOptionModule
```

Tech debt / missing feature in module system: make this automatic when the path leads to an option tree instead of a single option.
(no action required here)
